summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for intractable nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dysphagia, and odynophagia, all stemming from severe radiation esophagitis related to prior treatment for tracheal cancer. Despite a recent hospitalization and treatment with high-dose pantoprazole and fluconazole, her symptoms progressed, leading to poor oral intake and dehydration. A CT scan showed worsening esophageal wall thickening, and GI consultation confirmed she was not a candidate for dilation due to severe ulceration. A percutaneous endoscopic jejunostomy (PEJ) tube was placed to enable enteral feeding and allow the esophagus to heal. Her nausea and vomiting resolved post-procedure, and pain was managed with adjusted opioid dosing. A prednisone taper was initiated for rheumatoid arthritis, and nortriptyline was started for neuropathic pain. She was discharged home with nursing services, a detailed medication regimen, and plans for outpatient GI follow-up to reassess for dilation in several weeks.
